messages.subject: recordTable ::: using a web storage
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am developing a DT (interactive) table object generated from metags embbebed in photos from Jaguars. This table is contained in an html based on shiny. This app idea was to identify jaguars as individuals and when users add a new tagged photo, it will be updated and rendered easily. This table has a last column with a small image of the jaguar specimen.

I can run succesfully this app locally in my laptop, but I want to use the Qnap NAS (where I want to store all the pictures). I attached a screenshot below. I can share and access these photos using the NAS as a "cloud storage", but... could I run my app to explore the photos located there? Futhermore, I want to render the small images from the NAS as the original table.

#==========#==========#==========#==========#==========#==========#
This is my original (succesfully) script lines

# Define the directory
wd_images_ID <- "D:\\home\\ignacio\\Pictures\\ID_yaguarete_Test"

# Record images
rec.db.species0 <- recordTable(inDir = wd_images_ID, IDfrom = "directory")

# Set as tibble
rec.db.species0_tbl <- as_tibble(rec.db.species0)

#==========#==========#==========#==========#==========#==========#
This is my not working script lines

# Define the directory
wd_images_ID <- "https://www.myqnapcloud.com/share/6ff86i754l6p702tv71w5zcb_b9336hii4642205p0uswyz911z6522ij?session_id=2%7C1%3A0%7C10%3A1636655527%7C19%3Asession_portal_goto%7C48%3AOTMyYTIwNjUtYmFjNy00ZWI1LTk4ZWEtODNjM*********f0547017#/home"

# Record images
rec.db.species0 <- recordTable(inDir = wd_images_ID, IDfrom = "directory")
> Warning: timeZone is not specified. Assuming UTC
Error: Could not find inDir:
https://www.myqnapcloud.com/share/6ff86i754l6p702tv71w5zcb_b9336hii4642205p0uswyz911z6522ij?session_id=2%7C1%3A0%7C10%3A1636655527%7C19%3Asession_portal_goto%7C48%3AOTMyYTIwNjUtYmFjNy00ZWI1LTk4ZWEtODNjM*********f0547017#/home

# Set as tibble
rec.db.species0_tbl <- as_tibble(rec.db.species0)

#==========#==========#==========#==========#==========#==========#
So far, I have two main questions:

1- How can I implement camtrapR::recordTable function to a web storage? Is it possible?
2- If this option cannot be done, what other alternative could I implemented?

Thanks in advance!!

Ignacio

messages.subject: Re: recordTable ::: using a web storage
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ignacio,
this is an interesting application, and quite neat that you can show the images inside the table.

Unfortunately I don't have experience with images on web folders, so I can't answer properly. It probably depends how the data are stored on the cloud. Is it a directory structure just like on the local drive? If yes then I think it should theoretically be possible to run recordTable() on the server. Or is it some sort of database?

Are you using RStudio server to work with the cloud data?

A different approach, not directly related to your question: One can also configure digiKam to work with a remote MySQL database (instead of the default, local sqlite database), which would allow different users to access images from a cloud storage solution. But again I don't have experience with that, and it's marked as "experimental" in digiKam, even though it has been around for 10 or more years.

Sorry I can't be of more help here. If you learn more please feel free to share.
Thank you, best regards and apologies for the late reply.
Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: Error in cameraOperation
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
please see
data("camtraps")
camtraps

for an example. In the error message you received, X stands for a number, e.g. "1" (or possibly higher numbers, but always starting with 1).
So you want columns that are called
"Problem1_from" and  "Problem1_to" as in the example. If there were additional malfunction periods, the columns would be called "Problem2_from" and  "Problem2_to" etc.
Best,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: recordTable ::: using a web storage
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ignacio,
I can only speak from experience with Dropbox, which works fine if the data are on the user's machine (i.e., the folder is synchronised and smart sync is set to "local"). Then the data are synchronized on the user machine they behave like any other folder and one can run recordTable without problems.
With GDrive I suppose it's the same if the user synchronises the folder. I don't know about NAS.

In any case, it's crucial that the data are on the local machine. The error message (Could not find inDir) suggests that the folder does not exist locally, hence the function can't do anything.

If it is not not possible to have the users download / synchronise the data to their machines, then hosting it on the server only and using RStudio Server may be an alternative, but I don't have experience with that.

Best, Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: recordTable ::: using a web storage
messages.body_plain:
Dear Jürgen

Yes, I could realize that, that it is necessary that if or if it is a local directory. I tried the "exifr" package and the exact same thing happens. This package also requires the photos to be stored locally.

There is currently a boom in direct data collection from citizen science apps, shiny mobile development, classic shiny interactive apps, and enhance of internet connectivity where trap cameras are placed. In addition, the use of NAS and cloud backups (eg, amazon web services) is growing, so I think that if the camtrapR package could scan photos not saved locally, it would be a unique, novel and highly valuable feature within the R community. I leave this idea to you as a constructive suggestion to realize this possibility for your camtrapR package.

Jürgen, again thank you for your contribution in time and work in the community of R.

Best, Ignacio
